clues.text: Serving under Nebuchadnezzar's chief official, he would not defile himself with the king's food or wine.
He went in before Nebuchadnezzar and asked for time so he could give the king the interpretation of his dream.
At King Belshazzar's banquet, he read the writing that said the king was weighed on the scales and found deficient.
After King Darius signed a decree, he still knelt and prayed three times a day by windows open toward Jerusalem.
King Darius sealed a stone over the lions' den with his signet ring, so nothing concerning him could be changed.
Ezekiel named him with Noah and Job as men whose righteousness could save only themselves.
Jesus told His followers that this prophet had spoken of the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place.
